{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABX4BlkA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhBcHo4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 13, "title": "Automatically infer cartridge mappers from ROM content without an external database", "body": "## Problem

The current `Auto` cartridge option in `crates/msx-core/src/cartridge.rs` recognizes only plain 8/16/32/48 KiB AB-header ROM images. Any MegaROM requires a user to know whether it uses ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami, or Konami SCC, select the mapper in advanced options, and reselect the file. This is unintuitive even though these four ROM-only mapper implementations already exist (#8), and MSX1/MSX2 machine selection is now available (#11).

A public ROM hash database exists in other emulator projects, but its redistribution/licensing status has not been established for this MIT-licensed repository. **This Issue deliberately implements independent ROM-content heuristics only**; do not copy or embed another emulator's database, code, or curated mappings.

## Expected outcome

With **Cartridge mapper → Auto** (the default), selecting a supported plain ROM or MegaROM should inspect the local ROM contents and automatically choose a likely supported cartridge mapper **when there is sufficient evidence**, then load/reset the machine normally. The user should not have to select a mapper for confidently identifiable images.

The detector must be written independently in Rust with deterministic, explainable behavior. The supported inference targets are **Plain, ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami, and Konami SCC**. Uncertain or unsupported images must produce a useful explanation and offer manual selection, rather than silently loading with an arbitrary guess or claiming that a loaded ROM is a successfully running game.

No network service or ROM database is required, and no ROM contents or hashes are uploaded.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository: `takahirox/msx-rust`, default branch `main`.
- Existing paths include `crates/msx-core/src/cartridge.rs` (mapper selection/validation), `crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs`, `web/app.js` / `web/index.html` (picker and status), and `tests/browser.spec.js`.
- Reproduce: choose `Auto` and import a legitimate bank-switched ROM above 48 KiB; the application currently returns an error telling the user to choose the documented mapper manually.
- Prior work: #8 added ROM-only MegaROM mappers without a fixed upload cap; #7 redesigned the interface; #11 added MSX2 machine support. Preserve those features.
- Hardware references and other publicly documented mapper behavior may inform the independent implementation. Do **not** port existing GPL heuristic source or derive/redistribute the openMSX software database.
- Distinguish mapper identification from required machine model, system BIOS/sub-ROM, SCC audio, and other hardware compatibility. Detection must not imply unsupported hardware has become available.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Independent, deterministic mapper detection

- [ ] Implement a focused, well-tested ROM-content detector in the Rust core. Handle correctly recognizable plain images and infer among the currently supported ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami, and Konami SCC ROM-only mapper types using structural evidence and probable Z80 writes to mapper register address ranges. Document the method, its assumptions, and why an address pattern is meaningful.
- [ ] Do not treat file size, cartridge publisher, or the `AB` signature alone as sufficient to identify a MegaROM mapper. Reduce false positives caused by incidental instruction bytes inside data, shared register addresses, or common generic writes; use weighted/competing evidence rather than an unconditional first-match rule.
- [ ] Return a machine-readable detection outcome including the selected mapper (if confident), a meaningful confidence/ambiguity indication, and an explanation or candidate hints when detection is uncertain. Exact confidence scoring is an implementation choice, but thresholds and tie-breaking must be documented and deterministic.
- [ ] Validate the proposed mapper against the existing mapper/ROM format rules **before** altering the active machine. If no supported candidate is sufficiently credible, do not force a guess: keep the current ROM and active machine state intact, and explain how to select a mapper manually. Reject malformed/empty images safely.
- [ ] Keep the existing explicit `Plain`, `ASCII8`, `ASCII16`, `Konami`, and `Konami SCC` options as true manual overrides. Selecting an explicit mapper bypasses heuristic choice but retains format and safety validation.
- [ ] Do not make detection dependent on a proprietary ROM sample, external API call, downloaded/hash-indexed ROM database, or runtime network access. Keep ROM bytes local in the browser and preserve the current efficient Wasm upload path.
- [ ] Ensure Auto behaves consistently under MSX1 and MSX2 profiles without changing the machine model merely because of a mapper guess. Loading under the correct mapper does not prove a commercial cartridge can boot with the available BIOS/hardware.

### Browser UX and documentation

- [ ] Make `Auto` the low-friction default for plain and supported bank-switched cartridges. On successful import, clearly display which mapper was inferred (and that it is an estimate when applicable) instead of silently presenting it as verified ROM identity.
- [ ] When detection is ambiguous or unsuccessful, show actionable, concise feedback and keep the user's selected/loaded ROM, running session, and manual mapper controls intact. Users can retry by selecting a mapper and re-importing the same local file.
- [ ] Update advanced ROM help, status/error messages, README, and compatibility notes to explain automatic inference, the manual override, supported formats, and known limits. Remove outdated text claiming Auto recognizes only plain 8–48 KiB ROMs.
- [ ] Preserve the current GitHub Pages build, local-only file handling, cartridge reset/ejection, MSX1/MSX2 mode switching, and unrelated UI functionality. No unauthorized ROM assets or game identifiers are added to the distribution.

### Automated tests and review

- [ ] Add original, redistributable ROM fixtures or builders with deliberate mapper-register access patterns for Plain, ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami, and Konami SCC; verify expected classifications and confidence handling. Include ambiguous/conflicting and unrelated byte-pattern negative cases, malformed inputs, and regression coverage for existing manual selection.
- [ ] Add browser Playwright tests that actually import original MegaROM fixtures with `Auto` through the file picker/Wasm API, check the detected mapper and observable cartridge execution, and verify that failed/ambiguous attempts do not replace a running cartridge or corrupt state. Keep existing MSX1/MSX2 and `/msx-rust/` tests passing.
- [ ] Run and report applicable `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test` checks. Update screenshots when useful. Avoid claiming universal accuracy from only synthetic fixtures.
- [ ] Keep the change focused and consistent with the repository's English Issue → implementation → PR → review → merge flow. **Automated validation is the pre-merge gate**; no human copyrighted-game testing or subjective confirmation may block approval or merge.

## Optional validation

- Following merge, the owner may try lawfully obtained real cartridges (including known Konami/ASCII titles), report incorrect guesses or remaining boot incompatibilities, and open separate follow-up Issues.
- A separately licensed ROM hash database may be evaluated in a future Issue only after redistribution rights are established; it is not part of this Issue.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] Confirm GitHub Pages publishes the merged build and the deployed `Auto` picker boots an independently authored MegaROM test fixture without manual mapper selection. Record the published run/URL and actual results. This verification must not be a pre-merge approval gate; new compatibility defects can be tracked as follow-up Issues.
